canonicalJson.appliesTo: Every signed payload and every digest input (request bodies, envelopes embedded in other envelopes such as retry.revocation).
canonicalJson.notes: JCS is chosen over a bespoke canonicalizer specifically so unrelated, actively maintained JCS libraries exist for both .NET and JS/TS, removing whitespace/key-order/number-formatting disagreement as a source of cross-runtime signature mismatch.

requestSigning.description: Every mutating relay request signs a newline-joined base string over the request itself, independent of any envelope-level signature.
requestSigning.normalizedPath: Absolute path only (no scheme/host/query), percent-encoding normalized to uppercase hex digits, no trailing slash except '/'.
requestSigning.signatureAlgorithm: ECDSA-P256-SHA256, raw (r||s) format, 64 bytes, base64url-encoded without padding (86 characters).

nonce.scope: Unique per (deviceKeyId, nonce) pair; the relay rejects a reused nonce within the replay window regardless of timestamp.

capabilitySecrets.encoding: base64url without padding (43 characters) when transmitted; server stores only SHA-256(secretBytes) as capabilityId's paired hash.
capabilitySecrets.comparison: Constant-time hash comparison; the relay never logs or echoes the raw secret.
capabilitySecrets.invitationIdException: invitationId specifically uses 128 bits (base64url without padding, 22 characters) instead of the 256-bit default - it is single-use, short-lived (invitationExpirySeconds), and already bounded by the deviceInvitationCreate rate limit, so the smaller size still leaves guessing infeasible. Every other capability id (e.g. catalog requestId) keeps the 256-bit default.

proofDigest.description: The acceptance envelope's proofDigest is an opaque, single-use, exact-match token (compared for equality against the acknowledgement tell's carried value, never used as a content-integrity hash) - not a SHA-256 digest despite the name.

pairEpoch.type: non-negative integer, starts at 0 for a pair's first activation
pairEpoch.rule: Incremented every time a pairIdHash is re-activated after a prior revocation. Revocations, catalog requests/responses, and retries are valid only for the pair epoch they were issued under; anything from an older epoch is rejected.

monotonicSequence.revocationSequence: Strictly increasing per pairIdHash across all epochs; the relay and both clients reject a revocation whose sequence is not greater than the highest one already accepted for that pair.
monotonicSequence.snapshotId: Strictly increasing per pairIdHash within a pair epoch; the Owner rejects a catalog-response whose snapshotId is not greater than the last snapshot it successfully imported for that pair epoch.

keyAgreement.note: The Owner's ephemeral ECDH key travels in catalog-request; the Sub's ephemeral ECDH key travels in catalog-response. Neither is reused across requests.
keyAgreement.pushNote: catalog-push: the Owner publishes a signed catalog-mailbox-key receive key (rotated on every consume, so each decrypts at most one delivered snapshot); the Sub pairs it with a fresh ephemeral key per upload.

kdf.pushInfo: "oathbound-relay-catalog-push-v1" || pairIdHash || receiveKeyId, UTF-8 concatenation (catalog-push only; catalog-response keeps the info above)

aead.nonceGeneration: CSPRNG per encryption, never reused for the same derived key
aead.additionalAuthenticatedData: JCS(catalog-response envelope with ciphertextDigest/nonce/signature fields removed), binding ciphertext to its envelope metadata

compression.order: compress plaintext, then encrypt the compressed bytes; ciphertextDigest is SHA-256 of the final ciphertext (compressed+encrypted+tag)

pairingCode.description: collar/pairing code invitations. The code is shown and typed as Crockford base32 in groups of four; it is normalized (uppercase, dashes/spaces removed, I/L -> 1, O -> 0) and its UTF-8 bytes are the HKDF input keying material. The relay only ever sees SHA-256(lookupId).
pairingCode.lookupIdEncoding: base64url without padding (43 characters) of the HKDF output; used as the invitationId capability of a code invitation.
pairingCode.characterBlob: AES-256-GCM, 12-byte random nonce, plaintext = JCS of {name, world, triggerPhrase?}, AAD = UTF-8 of "oathbound-pair-code-v1|" + invitationId + "|" + ("inviter" | "accepter").

recoveryCode.description: collar/pairing-recovery. Same normalization and HKDF parameters as pairingCode; the relay only ever sees SHA-256(backupId).
recoveryCode.backupBlob: AES-256-GCM, 12-byte random nonce, plaintext = the client's backup JSON, AAD = UTF-8 of "oathbound-backup-v1|" + backupId.
